newsitem.title: THAILAND: Top Thai leaders agree on IMF loans-c.bank chief.
newsitem.headline: Top Thai leaders agree on IMF loans-c.bank chief.

text.p: Thailand's prime minister and finance minister have agreed in principle since July 22 to tap loans from the International Monetary Fund (IMF), central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond said on Monday.

"No specific figures had been agreed. We (Thailand and IMF) only discussed it in broad principle," he told reporters in the first statement from the authorities signalling that Thailand had made a decision to accept financial assistance from the IMF.
Any loan taken from the IMF would be channelled to assist the whole economy and not to bail out any specific sector, Rerngchai said.
Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya has so far declined to disclose if Thailand will seek IMF loans or a standby credit line to help it beat a liquidity crunch.
He told reporters on Monday that the government would have to study whether IMF financial aid was necessary as part of a rescue package for the ailing national economy.

Thailand is going through its worst economic crisis in over a decade and economists as well as local businesses have asked the government to bring in the IMF to help the country overcome its problems.
Thanong has confirmed that he is meeting a five-member IMF team for advice.
